clue.text: Is in possession of foot covering for something to kneel on

parts.note: to be in possession of something is to have it, so 'is in possession of' gives has
a sock is a covering worn on the foot

explanation.surface: Someone owns a piece of footwear, apparently for kneeling on.
explanation.definitionFit: A hassock is a firm cushion used in church for kneeling during prayer.

clue.text: See 6
Seat that's too low for some

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A complaint that a chair is too low for some people.
explanation.definitionFit: A stool is a simple seat with no back or arms.

clue.text: Jazz fan's hanging around nude nightclub

indicators.note: hanging around says the jazz fan's letters surround the next word

parts.note: cat is old slang for a jazz enthusiast; the 's stands for 'has'
nude means bare

explanation.surface: A jazz lover lingers near a naked performer in a nightclub.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabaret is a nightclub or restaurant offering live entertainment.

clue.text: Little fellow heard to be after duck roll for bishops

indicators.note: to be after says the sound-alike piece follows the duck

parts.note: to duck is to dip, as under water

indicators.note: heard says the little fellow's word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a tyke is a small child, a little fellow

explanation.surface: A small boy is heard queuing behind a duck for a bread roll.
explanation.walkthrough: The piece said aloud is TYKE, entered as TYCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A diptych was a two-leaved tablet on which the names of bishops and others to be remembered in the liturgy were listed.

clue.text: Go 'Coo!'. Flaunt busty novel choice, excited with very little showman's shout

indicators.note: excited says the letters of the preceding words are stirred up into a new order

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for very, as in v. small, so very little gives the single letter

explanation.surface: A suggestive caption urges a reader to gasp at a racy, showy novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' acts on GO COO FLAUNT BUSTY NOVEL CHOICE plus V (from 'very little'), 28 letters in all, making the whole answer across five lights.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the famous song line of a fairground coconut-shy showman calling customers to throw at his stall.

clue.text: Book 20 cross-fertilised hangers-on in wine country?

definitions.meaning: a famous novel by John Steinbeck
20 is the answer bunch of; fruit that hangs on vines in wine country, made cross, reads as a bunch of angry fruit

explanation.surface: A book about crossbred clusters of fruit hanging in vineyards.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is cryptic: hangers-on in wine country are what grow on vines, and cross means angry, so angry vine fruit is the novel's title.
explanation.definitionFit: The title names Steinbeck's 1939 novel about Dust Bowl migrants travelling to California.

clue.text: Painter shows impudence after tea

indicators.note: after says the impudence word follows the tea word

parts.note: cha (or char) is British slang for tea
gall means cheek or impudence

explanation.surface: An artist behaves cheekily once teatime is over.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces go in answer order: CHA then GALL.
explanation.definitionFit: Marc Chagall was a Russian-French modernist artist, a well-known painter.

clue.text: See 17
See 6
I'm depressive and getting slower

parts.note: read literally, a car control speaks: it is depressed (pushed down) by a foot, and pushing it makes the vehicle go slower

explanation.surface: A gloomy person admits to slowing down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depressive' looks like a mood, but it means something that gets pressed down underfoot.
explanation.definitionFit: The foot-operated control in a car that applies the brakes is pushed down to slow the vehicle.

clue.text: Reporter's one who sticks his nose in a fruit tree

indicators.note: a reporter speaks, so the meddler word is taken by its sound

parts.words: one who sticks his nose in
parts.note: someone who sticks their nose in is a meddler, a busybody

explanation.surface: A journalist is a nosy busybody poking about in an orchard.
explanation.definitionFit: The medlar is a small tree grown for its brown fruit, eaten when half-rotten.

clue.text: A green nut (European) for sprinkling into cake mix

indicators.note: sprinkling into says the European letter and the word for are scattered among the cake letters
mix says those combined letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A recipe: scatter a European green nut into the cake mixture.
explanation.walkthrough: E, FOR and CAKE together are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Green means environmentally minded and nut means fanatic, so a green nut is an environmental zealot.

clue.text: Accelerating machine taking years off companion without putting years on fool

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside says the shortened companion goes around the next piece
taking years off says the letter Y is removed from the companion word

parts.note: a crony is a close companion
a clot is British slang for a fool

explanation.surface: A machine that removes years from a companion's age but adds them to a fool's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking years off' leaves CRON; 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, so CRON wraps the years-and-fool piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A cyclotron is a particle accelerator that speeds charged particles round a spiral path.

clue.text: This is a blow below the belt, or I'm a Dutchman!

definitions.text: This is a blow below the belt, or I'm a Dutchman!

parts.words: This is a blow below the belt, or I'm a Dutchman!
parts.note: read in two halves: a punch that lands low is a ..., and a native of the Low Countries such as Holland is a person from flat low land

explanation.surface: An exclamation of disbelief at a foul punch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or I'm a Dutchman' is a British idiom of disbelief, here taken literally.
explanation.definitionFit: A lowlander is someone from low-lying country, such as a Dutchman from the Netherlands.

clue.text: See 22
'Hey', one waves: mad, mad greengrocers would tell you this in the war

definitions.text: greengrocers would tell you this in the war

indicators.note: mad says the letters of hey, one and waves are crazily rearranged

parts.note: bananas is slang for mad or crazy

explanation.surface: A greengrocer shouting and waving wildly during wartime shortages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mad' as the anagram signal turns HEY ONE WAVES into the first eleven letters; the second 'mad' supplies the final word.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1920s song title became a catchphrase for shortages, as fruit was unavailable to shopkeepers during the Second World War.

clue.text: Eager to break tip off sword at induction

indicators.note: to break says the eager word bursts into the middle of the shortened sword
tip off says the end letter of the sword is cut off

parts.note: an epee is a fencing sword
agog means eager

explanation.surface: Someone keen to snap the point off a sword at a ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip off' leaves EPE; 'to break' means the eager word bursts into it. 'induction' suggests a ceremony but is the logic term.
explanation.definitionFit: Epagoge is the logician's term for induction, reasoning from particular cases to a general rule.

clue.text: Financial art of restaurant almost replacing one in soap

indicators.note: replacing says one letter of the soap word is swapped out for the restaurant piece

parts.note: Camay is a brand of soap
A is one, as in a single thing

indicators.note: almost says the restaurant word loses its last letter

parts.note: a bistro is a small restaurant

explanation.surface: A soap opera about a restaurant's money-handling skills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' makes BISTR from BISTRO, which replaces the second A of CAMAY. 'soap' looks like television drama but is the brand.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambistry is the study or practice of foreign exchange, a branch of financial expertise.

clue.text: See 6
Knock what's said on departing into desert

indicators.note: into says the departing words go inside the desert word

parts.note: to rat is to desert or betray
ta-ta is a casual British goodbye

explanation.surface: Someone knocks to say goodbye before leaving for the desert.
explanation.definitionFit: Rat-a-tat imitates the sound of repeated knocking on a door.

clue.text: Unique cooker given the same name twice?

definitions.meaning: the one great cooking fruit, read as a single outsized cooking variety
a nickname for the city whose song says it is named twice, New York, New York

explanation.surface: A one-of-a-kind oven with a doubled name.
explanation.walkthrough: A cooker is a cooking variety of fruit, not an oven.
explanation.definitionFit: The nickname is for New York City, so good they named it twice.

clue.text: Fabric articles (three) put behind counter

indicators.note: put behind says the articles follow the counter

parts.note: a bar is a counter in a pub
three articles in a row: the indefinite a, the definite the, and a again

explanation.surface: Three items of clothing are stowed behind a shop counter.
explanation.definitionFit: Barathea is a fine woollen cloth, often used for suits and uniforms.

clue.text: Deny development from age 10

indicators.note: development from says the letters of the following pieces are reworked

parts.note: 10 written as a word is ten

explanation.surface: A child denies having grown up since the age of ten.
explanation.definitionFit: To negate a claim is to deny or nullify it.

clue.text: Dead one put down in King George?

definitions.text: Dead one put down in King George?

indicators.note: put down in says the one word is laid inside the king's letters, downwards in this down clue

parts.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George, as on British post boxes
taken as written

explanation.surface: A deceased person laid to rest beside King George.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: a dead one who has been put down. 'Dead' is part of that picture rather than giving letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A goner is someone dead or doomed beyond saving, a person who has been finished off.

clue.text: One immersed in spy book on every relaxing location

indicators.note: on in an across clue says the following piece comes after
immersed in says the numeral is dipped inside the spy and book letters

parts.note: James Bond is the fictional spy
I is the Roman numeral for one
each means every

explanation.surface: A spy novel read by everyone at a resort.
explanation.walkthrough: BONDI BEACH is a famous surfing beach in Sydney, Australia; the numeral sits between the spy and the book.
explanation.definitionFit: Bondi Beach in Sydney is a famous place to relax in the sun.

clue.text: See 6
Lords showing anger at the urinals?

parts.note: what one does at the urinals is pee
rage means anger

explanation.surface: Peers lose their temper in the gents.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces go in answer order: PEE then RAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: The peerage is the body of peers, the lords of the realm.
